header.title: Rip
header.description: Scratch or tear a veil that covers the child. The veil hides all the content and each cut opens a gap with a line of light, with debris (`particle`) flying off it. `variant` sets the cut (`gouge`, `tear`, `slash`, `claw`) and `trigger` how it's made (`drag`, `click`, or `always`). Here the effect is the control: the root receives the gesture. It uses the Particles layer for debris, so it needs `particles.css`.

playground.title: Playground
playground.description: Combine props and scratch or click the card. `lines` set to `auto` uses `1` (or `3` with `claw`).
playground.label: Scratch me

base.title: Basic scratch
base.description: With the defaults (`variant="gouge"`, `trigger="drag"`, `particle="spark"`) the veil covers the card and dragging opens a `16` px gouge with a line of light and sparks. Each new gesture replaces the previous one, and very long strokes drop their first points (`240` max). The root has `overflow: visible` so debris can leave its edges, and its radius rounds the veil and flaps. The root here has `tabIndex={0}`: Tab to it and press Enter or Space to throw a full cut through the center.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: `gouge` is a glowing gouge. `tear` rips the veil: after a long cut (over `28%` of the short side) it splits into two flaps that pull apart. `slash` is a straight thin cut. `claw` is three parallel gouges. These use `trigger="click"`: each click crosses the card through the point you pressed, and the hole in the veil opens at the same pace as the line draws.

image.title: On an image
image.description: The veil covers any content, like an image. Drag a long cut and release: with `tear` the veil opens and reveals the image.

triggers.title: Triggers
triggers.description: `drag` cuts while you drag. `click` throws a cut across the whole card from the click point. `always` repeats a cut on its own every `delay + duration × 2 + 280` ms. With `drag` and `click`, Enter or Space on the focused root (or on a button inside) throws a full cut through the center: the keyboard has no drag.

lines.title: Lines
lines.description: `lines` adds parallel cuts (`1` to `8`). It defaults to `1`, except `claw`, which uses `3`. Sparks are split across the lines.

gap.title: Gap
gap.description: `gap` is the distance between parallel cuts, in pixels. Default `10`. Ignored with a single line.

particles.title: Debris
particles.description: `particle` sets what flies off the cut: `spark` is light streaks, `star` sparkles, `confetti` paper bits with more spin and drop, and `none` just the cut. Events don't depend on debris: with `none`, `onRip` and `outRip` still fire with every cut.

customParticle.title: Custom debris
customParticle.description: `renderParticle` draws each piece: return only the visual and the library still positions and animates the wrapper. It receives the particle, with its `color`, size, and `id`.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: `color` is the cut's light (white by default) and, without `colors`, also tints the debris. `veilColor` is the veil's color. `colors` is the debris palette. Prefer tokens.

width.title: Cut width
width.description: `width` is the width of the hole in the veil, in pixels (minimum `2`). The line of light is `28%` of it (`20%` with `claw`). Without `width`, `intensity` sets it: `10`, `16`, or `24`.

duration.title: Duration and delay
duration.description: `duration` is how long the cut takes to draw with `click` and `always`, and how long debris flies. `delay` postpones the automatic cut; it doesn't affect `drag`.

intensity.title: Intensity
intensity.description: Without `width` or `count`, `intensity` sets the cut width (`10`, `16`, or `24` px), sparks per point (`3`, `5`, or `8`), and how far they fly (`22`, `34`, or `48` px). It also takes a number from `0` to `1`. Drag on each card.

asChild.title: On an element (asChild)
asChild.description: With `asChild`, the veil mounts straight onto the child (an `article` here), without an extra `div`. The child gets `position: relative` from the surface class, and the veil and flaps take its radius. With a void element like `` or ``, which can't have children, the effect falls back to the wrapping `div`.

state.title: Paused and disabled
state.description: With `trigger="always"`, `isPaused` freezes everything in place: the cut drawing, the hole in the veil, the flaps, the debris, and pending timers. Resuming continues from that point. `isDisabled` turns the effect off and hides the veil, so the child stays visible and interactive.

callbacks.title: Events
callbacks.description: `onRip` fires when a cut starts (on press with `drag`, with each `click` or keyboard cut, or on start with `always`) and `outRip` when the gesture or cut ends and the last debris lands, with the reason in `event.reason` (`drag` is reported as `hold`). Here the veil is semi-transparent so the button shows. Dragging doesn't capture the pointer, so the button gets its click; if you activate it with the keyboard, it also throws a cut through the center.

texts.body: Drag across the card to tear the veil, or try the button with the mouse or keyboard.

header.title: Rip API
header.description: Reference for props, inheritance, accessibility, CSS classes and variables, and exported types of `Rip`.

demos.title: Demos
demos.description: Playground and examples for each variant, trigger, and option.

import.title: Import
import.description: Import it from `@gem-org/gemffects/rip` with `particles.css` (the debris) and `rip.css` (the veil and cut), or from the package root if you already load `styles.css`.

inheritance.title: Inheritance
inheritance.body: Accepts HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> (except color) and forwards them to the root div (or the child, with asChild). onPointerDown, onClick, and onKeyDown run before the effect's internal logic. ref is merged with the internal ref that measures the root. The --gemfx-rip-* variables are only written inline when you pass the prop that sets them, and then they go after style.

items.control: The effect is the control: the root receives the gesture and sets cursor: crosshair, user-select: none, and touch-action: none with drag. Dragging is tracked with listeners on window, without capturing the pointer, so buttons inside get their click.
items.hidden: The veil is decorative (aria-hidden): it hides the content visually, but screen readers still read it. Don't use it to hide sensitive information.
items.keyboard: With drag and click, Enter or Space throw a full cut through the center: on the root if it's focusable (with tabIndex or asChild on a control) or when activating a button inside. Without a focusable element, the keyboard can't reach the effect.
items.reducedMotion: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce there's no debris and no transitions: the cut and the hole appear directly. With always, a single fixed cut shows. Events still fire.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: ignoreReducedMotion (or the gemfx-ignore-reduced-motion class on an ancestor) keeps the motion. Use it only when essential.
items.touch: With drag, touch can't scroll starting from the effect. disabledOnTouch ignores touches and restores touch-action: auto; mouse and pen keep working.

items.root: Root. `inline-flex`, `position: relative`, `isolation: isolate`, and `overflow: visible`. Defines the variables' defaults.
items.variant: Active variant. `claw` thins the line of light (`20%` of the width).
items.trigger: Active trigger. Not added with `isDisabled` or `isActive={false}`. `drag` sets `cursor: crosshair` and blocks selection and touch scrolling.
items.holding: Added while you drag a cut.
items.open: Added when `tear` has opened the flaps.
items.paused: Added with `isPaused`. Pauses debris; the line, the hole, and the flaps are frozen from JS at their current value.
items.inactive: Added with `isDisabled` or `isActive={false}`. Hides the whole layer (veil, line, and debris) with `display: none`.
items.surface: Wraps the child (`z-index: 0`). With `asChild`, the class goes on the child itself.
items.layer: Effect layer (`position: absolute`, `inset: 0`, `z-index: 1`, `pointer-events: none`, `aria-hidden`). Inherits the root's radius.
items.svg: SVG with the veil and lines. `overflow: hidden` and `border-radius: inherit` (from the layer).
items.veil: Veil rectangle (`fill: var(--gemfx-rip-veil)`), clipped by a mask with the cuts. Removed when `tear` opens.
items.trail: Line of light for each cut, with glow (`feGaussianBlur`) and a `stroke-dashoffset` transition.
items.cut: Stroke of each cut inside the veil's mask. It has the same transition as the line, so the hole opens in step with the drawing.
items.flap: The two `tear` flaps (`background: var(--gemfx-rip-veil)`, `border-radius: inherit`). They shift `18px` and rotate `5deg` in opposite directions, with a shadow in the cut color.
items.spark: Each piece of debris, inside the Particles layer (`--rip`, exit easing). `classNames.spark` goes on each one.

cssVariables.title: CSS variables
cssVariables.description: Defaults live on `.gemfx-rip`. Each one is written inline on the root only when you pass its prop; otherwise you can redefine it with a class. The flap ones go inline on each flap.

items.color: The cut's light. Set by `color`; white by default.
items.veil: Veil and flap color. Set by `veilColor`; defaults to a mix of `neutral-950` (78%) and `primary-800`.
items.stroke: Cut width in pixels; default `16px`. Written inline when you pass `width` or `intensity`. The line of light uses `28%` (or `20%`).
items.timing: Duration and delay of the line and hole transition; the flaps also use the duration. Written inline when you pass `duration` or `delay`.
items.flap: Offset and rotation of each flap when opening.

tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.description: Global variables Rip reads as defaults. You can redefine them on the root with a class.

items.spark: Default `spark` palette when you pass neither `color` nor `colors`. `star` and `confetti` use the Particles palettes.
items.easing: Easing for the line and flaps (fallbacks `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` and `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)`).
items.durationSlow: Default for `--gemfx-rip-duration` (fallback `700ms`). If you pass `duration`, the inline value overrides it.

content.title: Content
content.description: What content sits under the veil and where the effect mounts.

state.title: Trigger and state
state.description: How it cuts, how it pauses, and how it turns off.

items.asChild: Applies the effect to the single child, without a wrapping `div`. With void elements like `img` it falls back to the `div`.
items.variant: `gouge` is a glowing gouge, `tear` rips the veil open into two flaps, `slash` a straight cut, and `claw` parallel gouges.
items.renderParticle: Draws each piece of debris. The library still positions and animates the wrapper.
items.color: The cut's light; white by default. Without `colors`, also tints the debris.
items.width: Cut width in pixels (minimum `2`). Wins over `intensity`.
items.count: Sparks per cut point (`1` to `12`), split across lines. Wins over `intensity`.
items.lines: Parallel cuts, `1` to `8`. `claw` uses `3` when omitted.
items.gap: Distance between parallel cuts, in pixels.
items.intensity: Without `width` or `count`: `10` / `16` / `24` px wide and `3` / `5` / `8` sparks.
items.duration: How long the automatic cut takes to draw and how long debris flies.
items.delay: Delay before the cut with `click`, keyboard, and `always`.
items.trigger: `drag` cuts while you drag, `click` throws a cut from the click, and `always` repeats it on its own. With `drag` and `click`, Enter or Space throw a cut through the center.
items.isActive: Allows cutting. When `false`, clears the cut and hides the veil.
items.isPaused: Freezes the cut, the hole, the flaps, debris, and timers; ignores new gestures.
items.isDisabled: Blocks cutting, clears the cut, and hides the veil; the child stays visible and interactive.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: Keeps debris and transitions even when the user prefers less motion. Only when essential.
items.disabledOnTouch: Ignores touch pointers; mouse and pen keep working.
items.onRip: Fires when a cut starts: on press with `drag`, with each `click` or keyboard cut, or on start with `always`. It doesn't depend on debris.
items.outRip: Fires when the gesture or cut (`delay + duration`) ends and the last debris lands, or on disable or unmount.
items.style: Inline styles for the root. Variables for the props you pass are written after it.
items.ref: Ref to the root (the `div`, or the child with `asChild`).
